- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% to counteract pessimism bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at +10% above peak or apply decay factor to subsequent days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline after peak), model tends to lag; add 1–3 days of downward correction lag in forecast.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., >+0.3 in 3 consecutive days), model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast slope or add +3–5% bias toward higher end.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true outcome by 3–8% in early cycles; apply +3% baseline offset to initial 5–7 days of forecast.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (±0.5+ swings), model over-smooths; reduce forecast variance by 15–20% to match sentiment noise.
